([[Mountain Brook, Alabama]]) | college = [[LSU Tigers men's basketball|LSU]] (2019–2021) | draft_year = 2021 | career_start = 2021 | years1 = {{nbay|2021|start}}–{{nbay|2022|end}} | team1 = [[Portland Trail Blazers]] | years2 = {{nbay|2023|start}}–{{nbay|2024|end}} | team2 = [[Brooklyn Nets]] | years3 = {{nbay|2025|full=y}} | team3 = [[Philadelphia 76ers]] | years4 = {{nbay|2026|start}}–present | team4 = [[New Orleans Pelicans]] | highlights = * First-team All-[[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] – [[Associated Press|AP]] (2021) * Second-team All-SEC – Coaches (2021) * SEC All-Freshman Team (2020) * [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] ([[2019 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2019]]) * 2× [[Alabama Mr. Basketball]] (2018, 2019) }} '''Trendon Nelson Watford''' (born November 9, 2000) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). Watford was a standout high school player in [[Birmingham, Alabama]], winning both [[Alabama Mr. Basketball]] and Alabama [[Gatorade Player of the Year]] twice. A [[McDonald's All-American]] and consensus five-star recruit, he was one of the top players of the 2019 class. After playing two seasons of [[college basketball]] for [[LSU Tigers men's basketball|LSU]], Watford signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2021. His contract was converted to a standard contract in 2022, and he played two seasons with the Trail Blazers before being waived in 2023. That summer, he signed with the [[Brooklyn Nets]], where he played for two seasons. Watford joined the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] in 2025, where he reunited with his friend [[Tyrese Maxey]] and made the playoffs for the first time in his career. In 2026, he signed with the [[New Orleans Pelicans]]. ==Early life== Watford was born in [[Birmingham, Alabama]], to Ernest and Belinda Watford. His older brother, [[Christian Watford|Christian]], played for [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]] for four years{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/3126883/2022/02/14/by-keeping-tearful-promises-trendon-watford-found-a-role-with-the-blazers-immense-amount-of-joy-and-happiness/|title=By keeping tearful promises, Trendon Watford found a role with the Blazers: 'Immense amount of joy and happiness'|date=February 14, 2022|website=The New York Times|last=Quick|first=Jason|access-date=August 20, 2026}} before becoming a professional basketball player.{{cite news|url=https://www.theadvertiser.com/story/sports/college/lsu/2020/01/06/trendon-watford-lsu-tigers-basketball-forward-facts/2663733001/|title=Trendon Watford: 3 things to know about the LSU basketball forward|website=Lafayette Daily Advertiser|last=Laskey|first=Chastity|date=January 6, 2020|url-access=subscription|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241204133133/https://eu.theadvertiser.com/story/sports/college/lsu/2020/01/06/trendon-watford-lsu-tigers-basketball-forward-facts/2663733001/|archive-date=December 4, 2024}} Christian is nine years older than Trendon, who attended all of his brother's home games throughout his four years at Indiana, driving the seven hours from Birmingham to [[Bloomington, Indiana|Bloomington]]. In addition to attending games, Watford also saw closed practices and pregame, halftime, and postgame speeches, leading his brother to remark that "Trendon owned that place". His older sister, Elise, played [[volleyball]] at [[Samford University]]. Watford was very close to his uncle, Stanley "Kidd" Glover, who died of [[lung cancer]] in 2020. He credits his uncle for his competitive drive, and writes "RIP Unc Kidd" on his shoes. Always the biggest player on his team, Watford was coached by his father Ernest, who played him on the perimeter instead of positioning him near the [[post (basketball)|post]], and had his son do thousands of ballhandling drills. Watford was named to his high school [[honor roll]]. ==High school career== Watford played high school basketball for [[Mountain Brook High School]]. A highly touted five star prospect,{{cite web|title=Memphis basketball recruit Trendon Watford delays decision date|url=http://www.commercialappeal.com/story/sports/college/memphis-tigers/basketball/2019/04/15/memphis-recruit-trendon-watford-delays-decision-date/3473445002/|website=[[The Commercial Appeal]]|last=Hill|first=Drew|url-access=subscription|accessdate=April 15, 2019|date=April 17, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190416141655/https://www.commercialappeal.com/story/sports/college/memphis-tigers/basketball/2019/04/15/memphis-recruit-trendon-watford-delays-decision-date/3473445002/|archive-date=April 16, 2019|url-status=live|df=mdy-all}} Watford holds many Alabama state records, including the [[Alabama High School Athletic Association]]'s career rebounding record. He led Mountain Brook to three consecutive state championships from 2017 to 2019, being named Class 7A State Tournament MVP in all three of those years. He won back-to-back [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards]] for Alabama boys' basketball in 2018 and 2019, and was a finalist for the national award in the latter year after averaging 23.7 points, 11.2 rebounds, 3.6 assists, 2.5 blocks, and 2.1 steals. He was named to the [[2019 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|McDonald's All-American Game]]{{cite web|url=https://playeroftheyear.gatorade.com/poy/assets/writable/53968/2019_BBB_TWatford.pdf|title=Mountain Brook High School student-athlete named Gatorade Alabama Boys Basketball National Player of the Year|date=March 15, 2019|website=Gatorade Player of the Year|location=Chicago, Illinois|format=PDF|access-date=August 20, 2026}} and [[Jordan Brand Classic]]. He averaged 17 points and 8 rebounds on the [[Nike Elite Youth Basketball League]] circuit.{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/26789179/five-star-power-forward-watford-commits-lsu|title= Five-star power forward Watford commits to LSU|date=May 21, 2019|last=Borzello|first=Jeff|website=ESPN|access-date=August 20, 2026}} ===Recruiting=== A top-15 prospect in the class of 2019{{cite news|url=https://eu.commercialappeal.com/story/sports/college/memphis-tigers/basketball/2018/07/26/trendon-watford-penny-hardaway-mike-miller-memphis-tigers-basketball/838618002/|title=How Trendon Watford's family, and Mike Miller, gave Memphis basketball its shot at a top-15 recruit|website=The Commercial Appeal|last=Giannotto|first=Mark|date=July 26, 2018|url-access=subscription|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250722030815/https://eu.commercialappeal.com/story/sports/college/memphis-tigers/basketball/2018/07/26/trendon-watford-penny-hardaway-mike-miller-memphis-tigers-basketball/838618002/|archive-date=July 22, 2025|access-date=August 20, 2026}} and ranked as the No. 6 power forward and the No. 1 recruit from Alabama by [[ESPN]], Watford's final list included [[LSU Tigers men's basketball|LSU]], [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]], [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]], and Indiana, where his older brother Christian had played, with the first three, all of which he visited, being the front-runners. On May 20, 2019, he committed to [[Will Wade]] and LSU. At the time of his commitment, Watford was considered a [[one-and-done player|one-and-done]] prospect for the [[2020 NBA draft]], and was ranked No. 15 in ESPN's mock draft. {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2019}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = Trendon Watford | position = [[Power forward (basketball)|PF]] | hometown = [[Birmingham, Alabama|Birmingham, AL]] | highschool = [[Mountain Brook High School|Mountain Brook]] (AL) | feet = 6 | inches = 8 | weight = 210 | 40 = | commitdate = May 20, 2019 | scout stars = | rivals stars = 5 | 247 stars = 5 | espn stars = 5 | espn grade = 93 }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | 40 = | year = 2019 | rivals ref title = LSU 2019 Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = | espn ref title = 2019 LSU Tigers Recruiting Class | rivals school = lsu | scout s = | espn schoolid = 99 | 247 overall = 19 | rivals overall = 16 | espn overall = 19 | accessdate = January 29, 2019 | bball = yes }} ==College career== Heading into his freshman season, Watford was one of the 20 players named to the [[Karl Malone Award]] watchlist for the top collegiate power forward in the nation. In his debut for LSU, an 88–79 win over [[Bowling Green Falcons men's basketball|Bowling Green]], Watford scored 10 points.{{cite news |title=No. 22 LSU opens season with 88-79 win over Bowling Green |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401169810 |accessdate=November 14, 2019 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 8, 2018}} He had his first double double in college on November 19, 2019, scoring 12 points and grabbing 12 rebounds as LSU defeated [[UMBC Retrievers men's basketball|UMBC]] 77–50.{{cite news |title=LSU cruises to 77–50 victory against UMBC |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401169840 |accessdate=November 21, 2019 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 19, 2019}} Watford scored a career-high 22 points on January 25, 2020, in a 69–67 win over [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]].{{cite news |title=Watford scores 22 and LSU overcomes Texas rally 69-67 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401169710 |accessdate=January 25, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=January 25, 2020}} At the conclusion of the regular season, Watford was named to the SEC All-Freshman Team.{{cite press release|url=https://www.secsports.com/article/28877731/sec-announces-2020-men-basketball-awards |title=SEC announces 2020 Men's Basketball Awards |publisher=Southeastern Conference |date=March 10, 2020 |accessdate=March 10, 2020}} His strong performance in the SEC tournament led to his being monitored by the [[Portland Trail Blazers]]' director of [[data science]], Zach Williams. He averaged 13.6 points and 7.2 rebounds for LSU as a freshman. Following the season, Watford declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]].{{cite news |last1=Givony |first1=Jonathan |title=LSU freshman Trendon Watford entering 2020 NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/29026256/lsu-freshman-trendon-watford-enter-nba-draft |accessdate=April 14, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=April 12, 2020}} On August 3, Watford announced he was returning to LSU for his sophomore season.{{cite news |last1=Embody |first1=Billy |title=Trendon Watford to return to LSU for sophomore season |url=https://247sports.com/college/lsu/Article/NBA-Draft-Decisions-Trendon-Watford-to-return-to-LSU-for-sophomore-season-149824162/ |accessdate=August 4, 2020 |work=247 Sports |date=August 3, 2020}} He scored a career-high 30 points in a SEC Tournament championship game loss to [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]]. Watford averaged 16.3 points and 7.4 rebounds per game as a sophomore. In two [[NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] games, he averaged 11.0 points and 7.5 rebounds, and was named to the All-SEC First Team.{{Cite web|title=TRAIL BLAZERS SIGN TRENDON WATFORD TO TWO-WAY CONTRACT|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/trail-blazers-sign-trendon-watford-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=August 3, 2021|access-date=August 3, 2021}} Following the season, he declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]] and hired an agent, thus forgoing his college eligibility.{{cite news |last1=Guilbeau |first1=Glenn |title=LSU's Trendon Watford to hire agent, enter NBA Draft, though he is not expected to be picked |url=https://www.theadvertiser.com/story/sports/college/lsu/2021/04/08/lsu-basketball-forward-trendon-watford-leaving-team-entering-nba-draft/7137427002/ |access-date=June 19, 2021 |work=[[The Daily Advertiser (Lafayette, Louisiana)|The Daily Advertiser]] |date=April 8, 2021}} ==Professional career== ===Portland Trail Blazers (2021–2023)=== Heading into the [[2021 NBA draft]], Watford expected to be picked in the middle of the second round after working out for 11 teams. During the draft, no team expressed interest in him until the [[Brooklyn Nets]], who held the second-to-last pick of the draft, which his brother Christian cautioned against. After he went undrafted, [[Portland Trail Blazers]] head coach [[Chauncey Billups]], who had not held a pick in the draft, called Watford and expressed interest in signing him to a [[two-way contract]]. The call was Billups's first in an official role as Blazers head coach. Watford promised Billups "that he was going to come [to Portland] and work his butt off". Watford was signed by the Blazers to a two-way contract on August 3, 2021. After participating in [[2021 NBA Summer League|Summer League]] in Las Vegas, Billups recommended he lose weight, and Watford worked with his trainer to improve his conditioning. His focus impressed Billups, and he began to earn minutes early in the [[2021–22 Portland Trail Blazers season|2021–22 season]] after not playing in 18 of the team's first 20 games. In January 2022, the Blazers suffered injuries to their frontcourt, and Watford's versatility as a backup big man led to an increase in minutes.{{cite news|url=https://www.oregonlive.com/blazers/2022/02/portland-trail-blazers-trendon-watford-seizing-opportunity.html|title=Portland Trail Blazers' Trendon Watford seizing opportunity|last=Fentress|first=Aaron|date=February 2, 2022|url-access=subscription|website=The Oregonian|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250720103452/https://www.oregonlive.com/blazers/2022/02/portland-trail-blazers-trendon-watford-seizing-opportunity.html|archive-date=July 20, 2025|access-date=August 20, 2026}} By February, he had played in 22 consecutive games, averaging 5.5 points, 3.6 rebounds, and 1.2 assists in 15.3 minutes of playing time. His contract was converted to a standard deal on February 21, 2022. This deal was a four-year contact with the first two years guaranteed.{{cite news|url=https://www.oregonlive.com/blazers/2022/05/the-surprising-trendon-watford-earns-contract-and-place-in-teams-future-plans-trail-blazers-season-review-look-ahead.html|title=The surprising Trendon Watford earns contract and place in team's future plans: Trail Blazers season review, look ahead|last=Fentress|first=Aaron|website=The Oregonian|date=May 11, 2022|url-access=subscription|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221208173812/https://www.oregonlive.com/blazers/2022/05/the-surprising-trendon-watford-earns-contract-and-place-in-teams-future-plans-trail-blazers-season-review-look-ahead.html|archive-date=December 8, 2022|access-date=August 20, 2026}} Up to that point, he led all rookies with a [[field goal percentage]] of 59%, and ranked second in blocks, third in rebounds, fourth in games played, and fifth in points among two-way contract players.{{Cite web|title=TRAIL BLAZERS SIGN TRENDON WATFORD TO STANDARD NBA CONTRACT|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/trail-blazers-sign-trendon-watford-standard-nba-contract|access-date=February 21, 2022|website=NBA}} On March 12, he scored a career-high 27 points, along with six rebounds, in a 127–118 win over the [[Washington Wizards]].{{Cite web |title=Hart scores 44 as Trail Blazers top Wizards, end 6-game skid |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022101011 |access-date=March 27, 2022 |website=NBA}} Watford had a standout month of March, averaging 15.4 points, 6.7 rebounds, and 3.4 assists during the month prior to suffering a hyperextended left knee on March 26.{{cite news|url=https://www.oregonlive.com/blazers/2022/03/portland-trail-blazers-trendon-watford-suffers-hyperextended-knee-out-at-least-a-week.html|title=Portland Trail Blazers' Trendon Watford suffers hyperextended knee, out at least a week|last=Fentress|first=Aaron|website=The Oregonian|url-access=limited|date=March 27, 2022|access-date=August 20, 2026}} During March, the Blazers had been [[tanking]], which led Watford to play 31.5 minutes per game. The injury, which led to a bone [[contusion]], ended his rookie season. On July 17, 2022, Watford put up 19 points, seven rebounds, two assists, three steals, and one block to lead the Blazers to an 85–77 win over the [[New York Knicks]] in the [[2022 NBA Summer League]] championship match. He was later named the Summer League Championship Game MVP.{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/blazers-news-mvp-trendon-watford-reacts-to-portlands-2022-summer-league-championship/|title=MVP Trendon Watford reacts to Blazers' 2022 Summer League Championship|website=ClutchPoints|last=Azarly|first=Tomer|date=July 17, 2022|access-date=July 17, 2022}} Watford was also named to the All-NBA Summer League Second Team.{{Cite web |last=writer |first=SHELDON MICKLES {{!}} Staff |title=Three former LSU standouts among players earning All-NBA Summer League accolades |url=https://www.theadvocate.com/baton_rouge/sports/lsu/article_f11b4b92-0715-11ed-8af9-e3dc10a95121.html |access-date=2022-07-21 |website=The Advocate |date=19 July 2022 |language=en}} Heading into the [[2022–23 Portland Trail Blazers season|2022–23 season]], Watford was named by ''[[The Ringer (website)|The Ringer]]'' as a prospect who had "shown some flashes" but could play a bigger role in the future.{{cite news|url=https://www.theringer.com/2022/10/06/nba/nba-alignment-chart-2022-23-season|title=The NBA Alignment Chart|website=The Ringer|last=Mahoney|first=Rob|date=October 6, 2022|access-date=August 18, 2026|quote=This is a big moment for Nassir Little and Trendon Watford. That's both a great developing story for two young players who have shown some flashes, and less than a ringing endorsement for the state of Portland's bench.}} Watford suffered a hip flexor strain in training camp in September and aggravated it during the preseason. He missed his first eight games with the injury before returning in a November 5 loss to the [[Phoenix Suns]]. He played inconsistently in January, participating in only eight games, but gained a bigger role from February onward, averaging 10.5 points, 4.5 rebounds, and 3.0 assists for the remainder of the season. ''[[The Oregonian]]'' praised his energy and competitiveness.{{cite news|url=https://www.oregonlive.com/sports/2023/05/trail-blazers-season-review-look-ahead.html|title=Trendon Watford's upside immense: Trail Blazers season review, look ahead|website=The Oregonian|date=May 8, 2023|last=Fentress|first=Aaron|url-access=limited|access-date=August 20, 2026}} For most of the 2022–23 season, Watford played backup center behind [[Jusuf Nurkić]] and [[Drew Eubanks]], and backup power forward behind [[Jerami Grant]] and [[Justise Winslow]],{{cite news|url=https://www.oregonlive.com/blazers/2022/11/trail-blazers-trendon-watford-happy-to-be-back-in-action-i-missed-it-a-lot.html|title=Portland Trail Blazers' Trendon Watford happy to be back in action: 'I missed it a lot'|last=Fentress|first=Aaron|website=The Oregonian|date=November 6, 2022|url-access=subscription|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230204093043/https://www.oregonlive.com/blazers/2022/11/trail-blazers-trendon-watford-happy-to-be-back-in-action-i-missed-it-a-lot.html|archive-date=February 4, 2023|access-date=August 20, 2026}} but made an impact with his spirit in the locker room, playing a "glue guy" role both on and off the court. With the Blazers eliminated from playoff contention by the end of the season, Watford earned more playing time, starting at power forward several times, which helped expand his game. Due to his playmaking and connecting ability, Watford was considered an important part of the Blazers' future along with rookie [[Shaedon Sharpe]].{{cite news|url=https://portlandtribune.com/2023/03/24/hes-the-connector-trendon-watford-helps-bring-playmaking-and-light-to-the-blazers/|title='He’s the connector:' Trendon Watford helps bring playmaking and light to the Blazers|last=White|first=Austin|website=Portland Tribune|url-access=limited|date=March 23, 2023|access-date=August 20, 2026}} On June 30, 2023, Watford was waived by the Trail Blazers.{{cite web|title=Trail Blazers Waive Trendon Watford|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-waive-trendon-watford|website=NBA.com|date=June 30, 2023|access-date=August 6, 2023}} ===Brooklyn Nets (2023–2025)=== On August 3, 2023, Watford signed with the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{cite web|title=Brooklyn Nets Sign Trendon Watford|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-sign-trendon-watford|website=NBA.com|date=August 3, 2023|access-date=August 4, 2023}} He wore number 9 in Brooklyn.{{cite news|url=https://netswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/nets/2025/02/13/nets-jersey-history-no-9-trendon-watford-2023-25/78471287007/|title=Brooklyn Nets jersey history No. 9 - Trendon Watford (2023-25)|last=Quinn|first=Justin|website=USA Today|publisher=Nets Wire|date=February 13, 2025|access-date=August 21, 2026}} Then-head coach [[Jacque Vaughn]] played Watford at the [[point guard]] position behind [[Spencer Dinwiddie]], despite Watford having mainly played power forward and center during his time in Portland. He credits Brooklyn for unlocking and expanding his game.{{cite news|url=https://netswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/nets/2025/11/14/nets-credited-by-76ers-trendon-watford-for-unlocking-his-game/87279180007/|title=Nets credited by 76ers' Trendon Watford for unlocking his game|last=Phillips-Keaton|first=Sharif|website=USA Today|publisher=Nets Wire|date=November 14, 2025|access-date=August 21, 2026}} Entering [[restricted free agent (NBA)|restricted free agency]], Watford accepted a qualifying offer to make him an [[unrestricted free agent]] at the end of the next season, re-signing with Brooklyn on July 9, 2024.{{cite web|title=Brooklyn Nets Re-Sign Trendon Watford|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-re-sign-trendon-watford|website=NBA.com|date=July 9, 2024|access-date=July 9, 2024}}{{cite news|url=https://netswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/nets/2025/07/07/nets-cam-thomas-believed-to-not-have-much-of-a-market/84492400007/|title=Nets' Cam Thomas believed to not have much of a market|last=Phillips-Keaton|first=Sharif|date=July 7, 2025|website=USA Today|publisher=Nets Wire|access-date=August 21, 2026}} During the [[2024–25 Brooklyn Nets season|2024–25 season]], new head coach [[Jordi Fernández]] continued playing Watford at the [[point forward]] position due to his court vision and versatility. Fernández often ran [[post up]] plays involving Watford, and he had the best season of his career, averaging career highs of 10.2 [[points per game|points]] and 2.6 assists per game.{{cite news|url=https://www.inquirer.com/sixers/sixers-trendon-watford-nets-injury-hamstring-tyrese-maxey-quentin-grimes-nick-nurse-20251103.html|url-access=subscription|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251103152052/https://www.inquirer.com/sixers/sixers-trendon-watford-nets-injury-hamstring-tyrese-maxey-quentin-grimes-nick-nurse-20251103.html|archive-date=November 3, 2025|access-date=August 17, 2026|last=Mizell|first=Gina|date=November 3, 2025|title=Sixers' Trendon Watford flashes versatility in 'revenge win' over Nets|website=The Philadelphia Inquirer}} Watford suffered a left hamstring strain in training camp, which was the first of several left hamstring strains that kept him out of all but 17 of his first 52 games. The midseason trade of [[Dennis Schröder]] to the [[Golden State Warriors]] gave more primary ballhandling duties to Watford, who was successful in a larger role. Though the acquisition of [[D'Angelo Russell]] gave Brooklyn a new starting point guard, Watford's ballhandling decreased, but he continued strong playmaking from the power forward position.{{cite news|url=https://netswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/nets/2025/07/01/nets-lose-f-trendon-watford-to-76ers-in-2025-nba-free-agency/84429418007/|title=Nets lose F Trendon Watford to 76ers in 2025 NBA free-agency|last=Phillips-Keaton|first=Sharif|website=USA Today|publisher=Nets Wire|date=July 1, 2025|access-date=August 21, 2026}} After the Nets traded [[Ben Simmons]] at the trade deadline, Watford was anticipated to replace most of Simmons's playmaking.{{cite news|url=https://netswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/nets/2025/02/09/nets-trendon-watford-could-fill-void-left-by-ben-simmons/78378872007/|title=Nets' Trendon Watford could fill void left by Ben Simmons|last=Phillips-Keaton|first=Sharif|website=USA Today|publisher=Nets Wire|date=February 9, 2025|access-date=August 21, 2026}} Watford usually came off the bench during Brooklyn's rebuilding season in which they won only 26 games, playing at power forward behind [[Dorian Finney-Smith]] and [[Noah Clowney]] and at center behind [[Nic Claxton]] and [[Day'Ron Sharpe]], but he performed well during his starts, averaging 14.8 points, 5.5 rebounds, and 4.2 assists per game.{{cite news|url=https://netswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/nets/2025/05/04/nets-trendon-watford-2024-25-nba-season-highlights/83443206007/|title=Nets' Trendon Watford 2024-25 NBA season highlights|last=Phillips-Keaton|first=Sharif|date=May 4, 2025|website=USA Today|publisher=Nets Wire|access-date=August 21, 2026}} In a game against the [[Indiana Pacers]] on March 21, 2025, Watford was [[Ejection (sports)#Basketball|ejected]] and later fined $35,000 after an altercation in which he shoved Pacers players [[Andrew Nembhard]] and [[Myles Turner]].{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/44351912/nets-trendon-watford-pacers-myles-turner-fined-altercation|title=Nets' Trendon Watford, Pacers' Myles Turner fined for altercation|date=March 21, 2025|author=Associated Press|website=ESPN|access-date=August 17, 2026}} Tasked with creating more for himself and others, Watford's usage increased considerably in his second season in Brooklyn, and he played a career-high 20.8 minutes per game, but injuries limited him to a career-low 44 games. After the season, Watford entered free agency for the second year in a row, and he stated in his exit interview that he wanted to get what he deserved.{{cite news|url=https://netswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/nets/2025/04/16/nets-trendon-watford-seeks-to-get-what-he-deserves-in-free-agency/83127841007/|title=Nets' Trendon Watford seeks to get what he deserves in free-agency|last=Phillips-Keaton|first=Sharif|website=USA Today|publisher=Nets Wire|date=April 16, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250417032909/https://netswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/nets/2025/04/16/nets-trendon-watford-seeks-to-get-what-he-deserves-in-free-agency/83127841007/|archive-date=April 17, 2025|access-date=August 21, 2026}} The Nets chose not to re-sign Watford after the season, which was criticized for adding pressure on rookies such as [[Egor Dëmin]].{{cite news|url=https://www.si.com/nba/nets/onsi/news/ex-net-trendon-watford-drops-triple-double-raising-questions-about-brooklyn-call|title=Ex-Net Trendon Watford Drops Triple-Double, Raising Questions About Brooklyn’s Call|date=November 9, 2025|access-date=August 17, 2026|website=Sports Illustrated|last=Fox|first=Kyler}} === Philadelphia 76ers (2025–2026) === On July 2, 2025, Watford signed a two-year, $5.3 million contract with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{cite web | title=Philadelphia 76ers Sign Trendon Watford | website=NBA | date=2025-07-03 | url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/philadelphia-76ers-sign-trendon-watford | access-date=2025-12-06}}{{Cite web |title=Trendon Watford agrees to two-year deal with Sixers, report says |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/philadelphia/news/trendon-watford-sixers-nba-free-agency-2025/ |access-date=July 3, 2025 |website=CBS News |date=June 30, 2025 }} Head coach [[Nick Nurse]] had originally wanted to acquire Watford in a trade from the Nets the previous season before signing him in free agency.{{cite news|url=https://www.inquirer.com/sixers/sixers-raptors-takeaways-trendon-watford-triple-double-tyrese-maxey-joel-embiid-kelly-oubre-jr-nick-nurse-20251109.html|title=Sixers takeaways: Thriving in balanced attack; Trendon Watford’s triple-double and more from win over Raptors|last=Pompey|first=Keith|website=The Philadelphia Inquirer|url-access=subscription|date=November 9, 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260701020014/https://www.inquirer.com/sixers/sixers-raptors-takeaways-trendon-watford-triple-double-tyrese-maxey-joel-embiid-kelly-oubre-jr-nick-nurse-20251109.html|archive-date=July 1, 2026|access-date=August 18, 2026}} Watford was longtime friends with the team's star point guard [[Tyrese Maxey]]; they had talked on the phone the day free agency opened, hoping to soon play on the same team. His signing was praised by ''[[The New York Times]]'' as "one of the more effective signings on the margins a team can make". Watford replaced [[Guerschon Yabusele]], who left that summer in free agency;{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6492482/2025/07/14/sixers-roster-trendon-watford-joel-embiid/|title=Sixers being built to absorb the inevitable absence of star center Joel Embiid|website=The New York Times|last=Jones|first=Tony|date=July 14, 2025|access-date=August 17, 2026}} and provided size, length, versatility, and playmaking for the 76ers,{{cite news|url=https://www.nbcsportsphiladelphia.com/nba/philadelphia-76ers/trendon-watford-sixers-team-option-declined-nba-free-agency/739718/|title=Sixers decline Watford's option, forward now an unrestricted free agent|last=Levick|first=Noah|website=NBC Sports Philadelphia|date=June 29, 2026|access-date=August 17, 2026}}{{cite news|url=https://www.nbcsportsphiladelphia.com/nba/philadelphia-76ers/sixers-agree-to-sign-forward-trendon-watford-on-night-1-of-free-agency/673308/|title=Sixers agree to sign forward Trendon Watford on Night 1 of free agency|date=June 30, 2025|website=NBC Sports Philadelphia|last=Levick|first=Noah|access-date=August 17, 2026}} with his teammate and friend [[Quentin Grimes]] calling him a "[[Swiss Army knife]]". He was expected to reduce the team's dependence on its backcourt for capable ballhandling and on their often-injured center [[Joel Embiid]] for size and rebounding. As the only primary [[power forward]] on the 76ers' roster, he was expected to often receive playing opportunities as a key reserve off the bench.{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6667192/2025/10/01/nba-2025-preseason-reed-sheppard-john-collins/|title=Reed Sheppard, John Collins and other NBA 'hinge' players|date=October 1, 2025|access-date=August 17, 2026|last=Hollinger|first=John|website=The New York Times}} Watford suffered a [[hamstring injury]] in a September [[pick-up basketball|pick-up game]], missing the entirety of the 76ers' training camp and preseason, and the first three games of [[2025–26 Philadelphia 76ers season|the regular season]]. Due to his lack of chemistry with his teammates from the injury, Watford had a slow start to the season, scoring only two points in his debut on October 28.{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401809978|title=76ers rally in fourth, beat Washington 139-134 in overtime to remain undefeated|author=Associated Press|website=ESPN|date=October 28, 2025|access-date=August 17, 2026}} In his first game against his former Nets team on November 2, Watford continued to return to form, with an efficient 16 points, nine rebounds, and seven assists. Nurse maximized Watford's versatility by playing him as a point forward with the ball in his hands. On November 8, Watford recorded his first career triple-double in a 130–120 win over the [[2025–26 Toronto Raptors season|Toronto Raptors]], putting up 20 points, ten assists, and seventeen rebounds.{{Cite web |date=November 8, 2025 |title=76ers' Trendon Watford: Logs first triple-double of career |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/76ers-trendon-watford-logs-first-triple-double-of-career/ |access-date=November 9, 2025 |website=CBS Sports |language=en}} Following the game, Embiid compared Watford to [[Ben Simmons]].{{cite news|url=https://www.phillyvoice.com/sixers-news-analysis-trendon-watford-stats-contract-highlights-press-conference-interview/|title=Sixers year-in-review: Did Trendon Watford earn his spot?|last=Aaronson|first=Adam|website=PhillyVoice|date=May 28, 2026|access-date=August 18, 2026}} The game was his first [[Starting lineup#Basketball|start]] of the season, and began a short stint as Philadelphia's starting power forward. On November 25 against the [[Orlando Magic]], Watford suffered a left adductor strain and was expected to be out for at least two weeks.{{cite news|url=https://www.inquirer.com/sixers/sixers-trendon-watford-sidelined-adductor-muscle-20251126.html|title=Sixers' Trendon Watford out at least two weeks with thigh injury|url-access=subscription|date=November 26, 2025|last=Mizell|first=Gina|website=The Philadelphia Inquirer|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260113171929/https://www.inquirer.com/sixers/sixers-trendon-watford-sidelined-adductor-muscle-20251126.html|archive-date=January 13, 2026|access-date=August 18, 2026}} He returned to the lineup against the [[Washington Wizards]] on January 7, 2026.{{cite news|url=https://www.inquirer.com/wires/ap/sixers-wizards-score-joel-embiid-paul-george-tyrese-maxey-20260107.html|title=Joel Embiid and Paul George power the Sixers to a 131-110 win over the Wizards|url-access=subscription|date=January 8, 2026|last=Bracy|first=Aaron|website=The Philadelphia Inquirer|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260209093532/https://www.inquirer.com/wires/ap/sixers-wizards-score-joel-embiid-paul-george-tyrese-maxey-20260107.html|archive-date=February 9, 2026|access-date=August 18, 2026}} Watford initially had trouble returning to the rotation, but [[Paul George]]'s 25-game suspension for drug-related issues allowed him to earn a bigger role and more playing time in February. However, by April, he had fallen from the rotation again.{{cite news|url=https://www.inquirer.com/sixers/tyrese-maxey-paul-george-joel-embiid-nba-playoffs-20260405.html|title=The Sixers have a week to get ready for the playoffs. These are the five things they need to be working on.|url-access=subscription|last=Mizell|first=Gina|website=The Philadelphia Inquirer|date=April 5, 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260702132957/https://www.inquirer.com/sixers/tyrese-maxey-paul-george-joel-embiid-nba-playoffs-20260405.html|archive-date=July 2, 2026|access-date=August 18, 2026}} With the team affected by injuries in the early part of the season, Watford's ability to create for himself and others allowed him to handle the ball more and free Maxey to play off the ball. However, as the 76ers returned to health later in the season, Watford's ball-handling skills were used less as more capable ball handlers such as Embiid and [[Paul George]] returned from injury, and his lack of off-ball contributions limited his utility, as the 76ers had a −10.7 net rating when he played alongside their starting [[backcourt (basketball)|backcourt]] of Maxey and [[VJ Edgecombe]]. Due in part to his friendship with Maxey, Watford was a positive locker room presence, but poor shooting and defense combined with the hamstring and adductor injuries prevented him from establishing a consistent rotation role for the 76ers.{{cite news|url=https://www.phillyvoice.com/sixers-news-analysis-nba-free-agents-rumors-cap-sheet-contract-trendon-watford-stats-highlights-career-bio/|title=Report: Former Sixers forward Trendon Watford nearing move to Spain|last=Aaronson|first=Adam|website=PhillyVoice|date=August 3, 2026|access-date=August 18, 2026}} For the season, Watford averaged 6.5 points, 3.3 rebounds, and 2.5 assists in 53 games, at the end of the Philadelphia rotation. He scored efficiently on shots within 10 feet of the basket, which made up most of his shots,{{cite news|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nba/news/trendon-watford-signs-one-year-minimum-deal-to-join-new-orleans|title=Trendon Watford signs one-year minimum deal to join New Orleans|last=Helin|first=Kurt|date=August 17, 2026|access-date=August 17, 2026|website=NBC Sports}} but struggled to shoot from long range, with a [[Three-point field goal|three-point percentage]] of only 20%. The 76ers qualified for [[2026 NBA playoffs|the playoffs]] for the first time in Watford's career,{{cite news|url=https://www.inquirer.com/sixers/sixers-joel-embiid-tyrese-maxey-daryl-morey-nba-playoffs-offseason-20260512.html|url-access=subscription|title=The Sixers had an improved regular season and an up-and-down playoff run. Now, an interesting offseason awaits.|last=Mizell|first=Gina|website=The Philadelphia Inquirer|date=May 12, 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260513083430/https://www.inquirer.com/sixers/sixers-joel-embiid-tyrese-maxey-daryl-morey-nba-playoffs-offseason-20260512.html|archive-date=May 13, 2026|access-date=August 18, 2026}} but he was out of Nurse's playoff rotation, and saw little playing time compared to the starters and younger reserves such as [[Dominick Barlow]] and [[Justin Edwards (basketball, born 2003)|Justin Edwards]].{{cite news|url=https://www.inquirer.com/sixers/nba-first-round-series-vj-edgecombe-adem-bona-key-player-postseason-celtics-20260426.html|title=Sixers' playoff newcomers getting 'invaluable' experience in first series against Boston|url-access=subscription|last=Mizell|first=Gina|website=The Philadelphia Inquirer|date=April 26, 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260624000929/https://www.inquirer.com/sixers/nba-first-round-series-vj-edgecombe-adem-bona-key-player-postseason-celtics-20260426.html|archive-date=June 24, 2026|access-date=August 18, 2026}} The 76ers were criticized for using so many roster spots on "non-contributors" such as Watford.{{cite news|url=https://www.phillyvoice.com/sixers-news-analysis-lineup-depth-chart-roster-mike-gansey-daryl-morey-lebron-james-highlights-kcp-stats-nba/|title=On top of star-studded lineup, Sixers finally valuing back-end roster spots|website=PhillyVoice|last=Aaronson|first=Adam|date=July 30, 2026|access-date=August 18, 2026}} On June 29, 2026, the 76ers declined Watford's team option for the next season, making him an [[free agent (NBA)|unrestricted free agent]]. After his option was declined, Watford posted the [[Future (rapper)|Future]] song "[[Ain't Coming Back]]" on his [[Instagram story]].{{cite news|url=https://www.inquirer.com/sixers/sixers-nba-free-agency-trendon-watford-demar-derozan-guerschon-yabusele-20260707.html|title=If the Sixers don't land LeBron James, who should fill their final roster spot? Here are a few options.|url-access=subscription|last=Mizell|first=Gina|date=July 7, 2026|website=The Philadelphia Inquirer|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260812095315/https://www.inquirer.com/sixers/sixers-nba-free-agency-trendon-watford-demar-derozan-guerschon-yabusele-20260707.html|archive-date=August 12, 2026|access-date=August 18, 2026}} In free agency, Watford explored playing opportunities elsewhere,{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/49638189/trendon-watford-pelicans-agree-1-year-29m-deal|title=Sources: Trendon Watford, Pelicans agree to 1-year, $2.9M deal|date=August 17, 2026|access-date=August 17, 2026|website=ESPN}} including a reported deal offered to him in Spain by [[Valencia Basket]]. Via social media, Watford stated the report was false and he would be staying in the NBA.{{cite news|url=https://www.si.com/nba/pelicans/onsi/what-does-trendon-watford-signing-mean-pelicans-rotation-01m08scy7zpf|title=What Does the Trendon Watford Signing Mean for the Pelicans' Rotation?|last=Kimble|first=Terry|website=Sports Illustrated|date=August 17, 2026|access-date=August 18, 2026}} ===New Orleans Pelicans (2026–present)=== On August 17, 2026, Watford signed a one-year, $2.9 million minimum contract with the [[New Orleans Pelicans]], described by ESPN's [[Shams Charania]] as a "productive [[Two-way player#Basketball|two-way]] get". The deal, which brought the Pelicans to their full 15 players under contract, was the biggest signing of a mostly inactive offseason for the team. Watford was expected to play a veteran reserve role behind [[Zion Williamson]] and [[Derik Queen]], but could expand if either player was injured or if trades changed the New Orleans roster. Watford's signing raised questions for the Pelicans, as they continued to lack a legitimate starting [[center (basketball)|center]], and his lack of shooting ability was similar to Williamson and Queen. The Pelicans were expected to play lineups with Watford as a [[small ball (basketball)|small-ball]] center, allowing the team to use his connective playmaking ability. ==Player profile== Listed at {{convert|6|ft|8|in|m|2}} and {{convert|245|lb|kg}}, with a [[wingspan]] of {{convert|7|ft|2|in|m|2}}, Watford is a versatile playmaker, connector, and shot-creator, with skilled scoring ability in the [[post (basketball)|post]]. His unorthodox play style has been described as resembling that of a [[guard (basketball)|guard]] more than his listed position of power forward, and he most often plays as a point forward. He can also be deployed as a small-ball center who excels in the [[paint (basketball)|paint]], especially from the [[floater (basketball)|floater]] range. He has the unique ability to both bring the ball up the court like a point guard, and post up like a center. His ability to be a connector and ball mover has been compared to [[Nicolas Batum]].{{cite news|url=https://www.inquirer.com/sixers/sixers-trendon-watford-paul-george-suspension-nba-trade-deadline-20260208.html|title=Trendon Watford's versatility will become a major asset as the Sixers reshuffle their roster|url-access=subscription|last=Mizell|first=Gina|website=The Philadelphia Inquirer|date=February 8, 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260322173402/https://www.inquirer.com/sixers/sixers-trendon-watford-paul-george-suspension-nba-trade-deadline-20260208.html|archive-date=March 22, 2026|access-date=August 18, 2026}} Watford is known for his competitiveness and toughness, and his hustle was the main factor behind his entry into the Portland rotation off of a two-way contract. He excels in transition offense, where his ball-handling ability allows him to push the pace and exploit mismatches near the basket.{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6786378/2025/11/08/how-trendon-watford-is-finding-his-place-on-sixers-by-raising-his-ceiling-and-voice/|title=How Trendon Watford is finding his place on Sixers by raising his ceiling — and voice|website=The New York Times|last=Jones|first=Tony|date=November 8, 2025|access-date=August 18, 2026}} On March 6, 2026, while playing for the 76ers, Watford commented on his versatility: {{bq|I just try to go along with it. It's not a bad thing, being able to play a lot of positions... Some games I might come in at the four, backup four. Some games I might come in at the one. Some games I might come in [and replace Kelly Oubre Jr.] at the three. It just varies, and obviously it's a good thing to be able to play a lot of positions. But my job is to just stay locked in and be ready whenever my name is called, whatever position it may be.}} One of Watford's main weaknesses is shooting. Never a high-volume three-point shooter, Watford shot only 20% from three with the 76ers, which limits his usefulness when not handling the ball, although he increased his three-point volume in each of the preceding four seasons.{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6354256/2025/05/15/detroit-pistons-free-agency-nba-offseason-2025/|title=Pistons free agency: Naz Reid, Bobby Portis and 6 more players Detroit could target|last=Patterson|first=Hunter|website=The New York Times|date=May 15, 2025|access-date=August 18, 2026}} Though a switchable defender,{{cite news|url=https://www.theringer.com/2025/07/17/nba/nba-free-agency-signings-2025-best-deals|title=Six Tiny Deals That Might Tilt the 2025 NBA Season|last=Mahoney|first=Rob|website=The Ringer|date=July 17, 2025|access-date=August 18, 2026}} Watford is less skilled at the point of attack,{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6813698/2025/11/17/paul-george-philadelphia-76ers-return-from-injury/|title=Paul George nears his return to the 76ers. Here are 5 reasons why they need him|website=The New York Times|last=Jones|first=Tony|date=November 17, 2025|access-date=August 18, 2026}} and does not have a major presence defensively or in rebounding.
